advice: Hypothesis, unverified: test packing B into bounded K-by-column panels for the generated 512 path. For each 32-column output block, pack B[k, j:j+32] for K blocks of 32 into contiguous scratch, then compute that block across all output rows before reusing the panel. Adapt the SME2 load addressing to consume each packed panel; keep the A transpose and four ZA accumulators. Allocate scratch inside gemm, include packing and cleanup in timing, handle the final K and column blocks without out-of-bounds access, and fall back correctly if allocation fails. This may improve B reuse across output rows, but packing cost and the changed traversal may outweigh that benefit.
risks: The current generated assembly expects fixed full-matrix addresses, so this needs a small hash-bound assembly change to its B loads and output-block schedule. Pointer or panel-stride errors can corrupt results; scratch allocation can erase any compute gain. Keep ABI, FP32 arithmetic, streaming transitions, benchmark settings, tolerance, and BSD notice unchanged. This is a proposal, not measured evidence.
